source: NCERT Class VII, Social and Political Life II, Polity Ch. 6.

sections.heading: 1. Markets Around Us
points: A **market** is where **buying and selling** of goods and services takes place.
We buy from many kinds of markets — from a roadside vendor to a large shopping mall.
Goods reach us through a **chain of markets** connecting producers and consumers.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Markets
points: **Weekly market** — held on a fixed day; **cheaper** (no permanent shop, low costs, bargaining possible); sells everyday goods.
**Shops in the neighbourhood** — permanent, nearby, convenient, often on credit.
**Shopping complexes and malls** — many shops, branded goods, usually **costlier**.
Some markets are for **buyers directly (retail)**; others are **wholesale**.

sections.heading: 3. The Chain: Wholesale to Retail
points: **Wholesale trade** — buying goods in **large quantities** from producers and selling to retailers.
**Retail trade** — selling in **small quantities** directly to the final **consumer**.
Chain: **Producer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer** — the price rises at each step.
Not everyone buys/sells in the same markets — a **wealthy person** and a **poor person** shop very differently.

sections.heading: 4. Markets and Equality
points: Markets are not equal for all: **big businesses** and rich buyers have more power; **small sellers** earn little.
New forms: **online markets** let people buy from home (goods delivered).
The gains from a sale are **shared unequally** along the chain (see next chapter).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Market = place of buying & selling; goods reach us via a chain of markets.
Weekly market = cheaper (no fixed shop, bargaining); mall = costlier, branded.
Wholesale = large quantity to retailers; retail = small quantity to consumers.
Chain: Producer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer (price rises each step).
Online markets = buying from home.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Wholesale** = selling in **bulk** to shopkeepers; **retail** = selling in **small amounts** to consumers.
**Weekly markets** are usually **cheaper** than malls.
The market chain runs **Producer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer**.
Markets do **not** treat all participants equally — power and gains are unequal.
